question: A liquid cools from $70^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\text{C}$ in $5\text{ minutes}$ in a surrounding of temperature $30^{\circ}\text{C}$. What will be its temperature after the next $5\text{ minutes}$?
explanation: Using the average temperature method: $\frac{70 - 60}{5} = k\left(\frac{70 + 60}{2} - 30\right) \implies 2 = k(65 - 30) = 35k \implies k = 2/35$. For the next interval from $60^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $T_2$ in $5\text{ min}$: $\frac{60 - T_2}{5} = \frac{2}{35} \left(\frac{60 + T_2}{2} - 30\right) = \frac{2}{35}\left(\frac{T_2}{2}ight) = \frac{T_2}{35}$. Solving gives $7(60 - T_2) = T_2 \implies 420 = 8T_2 \implies T_2 = 52.5^{\circ}\text{C}$.

question: A body cools from $50^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $40^{\circ}\text{C}$ in $5\text{ minutes}$. The surrounding temperature is $20^{\circ}\text{C}$. In what further time will it cool down to $30^{\circ}\text{C}$?
explanation: First interval: $\frac{50 - 40}{5} = k(\frac{50+40}{2} - 20) \implies 2 = k(45 - 20) = 25k \implies k = 2/25$. Second interval from $40$ to $30^{\circ}\text{C}$ in time $t$: $\frac{40 - 30}{t} = \frac{2}{25}(\frac{40+30}{2} - 20) \implies \frac{10}{t} = \frac{2}{25}(35 - 20) = \frac{2}{25}(15) = \frac{30}{25} = \frac{6}{5}$. Thus $t = \frac{50}{6} = \frac{25}{3}\text{ minutes}$.

question: The initial temperature excess of a body over its surroundings is $T_i - T_0$. If the time constant of the cooling body is $\tau$, what is the temperature excess after time $t = \tau$?
explanation: The temperature excess at any time $t$ is given by $(T(t) - T_0) = (T_i - T_0)e^{-kt}$. At $t = \tau = 1/k$, the excess becomes $(T_i - T_0)e^{-1} = \frac{T_i - T_0}{e}$ accroding to the definition of the time constant.
